## The problem

Three gaps sat between the J3/J4 design intent and the code:

1. **No shared scrub implementation.** J3 §9.1 S-1…S-14 existed as design
   text and scattered helpers, not as the one module every transparency
   surface consumes (J3 T-6: a second scrub implementation is a defect).
   The never-exported list existed only as the exports layer's column
   projection.
2. **No publish-time secret scan.** A secret-shaped value committed into
   `web/dist`, a staged release tree, or an export tree would flow
   through `write_release_record` + remote sync undetected.
3. **`storage_tier='public'` by construction.** The P32.2 capture writer
   INSERTed the literal `'public'` on every synthetic and actual capture
   row — F-400's drift-by-default — and `/v1/evidence` trusted the
   recorded value: `source_uri` published for every capture,
   `retrieved_at` rendered date-only (S-10), and nothing tightened a
   row whose recorded tier outran its evidenced lane.

## What ships

- **`policy.transparency`** (new, ~880 lines, leaf package) — the closed
  vocabularies (`raw-ok|derived-only|link-only|restricted|unknown`
  lanes; `public|restricted|sealed` tiers; the P8 clear/recorded/sealed
  class sets; the S-4 error classes, S-11 gated reasons, S-13 robots
  outcomes, the J3 §3.5 never-exported list) and the S-rules as code:
  `strip_credential_query_params` + `scrub_headers` + `find_secrets`
  (S-1), `scrub_internal_locations`/`opaque_id` (S-2), `explicit_columns`
  raising `ScrubViolation` on a never-exported member (S-3/S-12 — an
  emit-layer defect, not data), `error_class`/`error_counts` (S-4),
  `strip_ip_addresses`/`contains_ip_address` (S-5), `scrub_source_url`/
  `upstream_host` (S-6 — host always; full URL only for raw-ok/
  derived-only past the gate), `scrub_personal`/`reviewer_role` (S-7),
  `tombstone_id` (S-9), `iso_utc` (S-10 — full ISO-8601 UTC, timezone-
  aware normalized, `+00:00`→`Z`; a date-only input raises), the
  `gated_source_row`/`robots_disclosure_rows` bounded emitters (S-11/
  S-13 with the GL-GATE-08 decision reference), and the composite
  `scrub_text`.
- **The publish secret gate (SIG-TRANSP-022)** —
  `ops.publish.assert_publish_set_secret_free` runs `find_secrets` over
  every file of the site tree AND the staged release tree AND the export
  tree, positioned after the allowlist/content/release-tree/attribution
  gates and **before** `write_release_record` and the mirror preflight.
  One hit aborts in dry-run and `--apply` alike; the refusal names file
  + pattern class, never the value; there is no override flag. Detector
  pattern classes: JWT `eyJ…`, AWS `AKIA|ASIA…`, private-key PEM blocks,
  `key=`-shaped hex secrets, `Authorization: Bearer …`, GCP API-key
  shapes — the detector's own specimens are runtime-assembled so this
  repo's scanners stay green.
- **Captured-tier derivation (NEW-2/F-400)** — `PgClaimSink` takes a
  `lane_resolver`; `_lane_and_custody` derives the tier from the
  source's redistribution lane + Part VIII class via `interim_lane`
  (custody posture, SPDX, reviewed `redistributable`, a recorded
  refusal) → `derive_storage_tier`: `raw-ok`+`clear` → `public`;
  `derived-only`/`link-only` → `restricted`; `restricted` lane or
  `P8-1`/`P8-2`/`P8-4` or **any unknown** → `sealed`. Both capture
  inserts (synthetic and actual) bind the derived tier — the `'public'`
  constant is gone. `connectors.sinks._registry_lane` maps the registry
  record → the basis fields (an unreviewed `redistributable=false`
  normalizes to `UNDETERMINED`, never a recorded refusal — same
  semantics as `_registry_rights`). The lane is the **interim**
  rights-record basis until row 313's `[redistribution]` fields land —
  a `public` write is unreachable today and that consequence is filed
  `D-P35.31-1` (recorded, never smoothed).
- **Honest `/v1/evidence`** — the capture SELECT joins
  `source_registry` + `rights_record` (LEFT — a legacy capture still
  answers) and serves `served_storage_tier` = the recorded tier floored
  by the lane at read time, **tighten only** (`more_restrictive_tier`
  normalizes to `sealed`; unknown can never relax). A pre-fix
  constant-`public` row is served at the derived floor labelled
  `tier_basis='derived_at_read'` + `recorded_tier='public'` — never a
  silent upgrade. `source_uri` emits only for the `public` tier
  (absent, not nulled); `retrieved_at` is a full ISO-8601 UTC timestamp;
  `bytes_available` keeps P34.25's `actual`-only truth.
- **`evidence.tiers`** — `CaptureMetadata` gains `tier_basis` +
  `recorded_tier` (additive, defaulted); `public_representation` gates
  `source_uri` on the served tier and carries the basis labels inside
  the sealed allowlist.

## The recorded boundary — what this does NOT do

- **A `public` capture is unreachable on the interim basis.** The rights
  record carries no Part VIII class field, so `derive_storage_tier` can
  never return `public` until row 313 lands the lane/class fields —
  `D-P35.31-1` (OPEN, cites BL-084). This is the ticket's own
  consequence ("a source whose lane/class the record cannot yet evidence
  derives sealed"), enforced in code, recorded in the register.
- **No migration, no backfill.** Pre-fix rows keep their recorded
  `public` tier (append-only); the API serves them tightened and
  labelled. The read-path floor is the honest interim posture.
- **No live verification.** `live_verification=false` — nothing
  published, no staging, no hosted check. The gate is proven on fixture
  publishes (planted secrets in all three trees abort before any write
  or remote call).
